## Repo conventions

- Use the Next.js App Router (`app/`). Prefer server components by default; only opt into client components via `"use client"` when needed.
- Style exclusively with Tailwind utility classes. Do not add inline `style` props or ad-hoc CSS unless the component is outside the design system.
- TypeScript strict mode is on. Never use `any`; prefer `unknown` + narrow at the boundary.

## Do / Don't

- Prefer small, focused diffs. One concern per PR or patch.
- Always show the exact test or typecheck command you ran and its result.
- When following a rule from this file, cite it by section heading so reviewers can audit.
- Do not refactor code unrelated to the task, even if it looks better.
- Do not add new dependencies without flagging the choice and reason.
- Favor server actions or RPC over ad-hoc fetches in client components.
- Do not paper over permission checks at the component level; they belong at the data layer.

## Never do this (unsafe)

- Never modify generated files (anything under `dist/`, `build/`, `.next/`, or marked `@generated`).
- Never edit lockfiles manually.
- Never commit secrets. Redact any `.env*` content that appears in logs or diffs.
- Never log, serialize, or include tokens/emails/IDs in Sentry or analytics payloads without scrubbing.

## File placement

- Pages go in `app/`. Route segments use `page.tsx`. Shared UI goes in `components/` or `src/components/`.

## Response expectations

- Before claiming work is complete, run the repo's typecheck and test commands and show the output.
- If the brief is ambiguous on a specific section, ask rather than guess. Cite the section heading.

## Component & design rules

- AppShell — Sidebar + TopBar + main content area; handles collapsed/expanded states.
- Sidebar — Nav with role-gated items; keyboard and screen-reader navigable.
- TopBar — Search, notifications, user menu.
- DataTable — Sortable, paginated, keyboard-navigable; supports row selection.
- EmptyState — First-run / no-data copy with suggested next action.
- FormDialog — Consistent modal with focus trap and escape-to-close.
- PermissionGate — Hides or disables UI based on the current user's role.

## Accessibility baseline

- All interactive elements must be reachable and operable with the keyboard alone.
- Focus must be visible at all times; never remove outlines without replacing them.
- Text contrast must meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text).
- Every form control has a programmatic label.
- Pages use proper landmark regions (header, main, nav, footer) and a sensible heading order.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for any non-essential animation.
- Modals trap focus and restore focus to the trigger on close.
- All interactive tables are keyboard-navigable (ArrowKeys, Home/End, Enter/Space).

## UX rules

- Every data surface has explicit loading, empty, error, and partial states.
- Destructive actions require confirmation and always present an undo path when feasible.
- Bulk operations show progress and a cancel affordance.

## QA guardrails

- Unit tests live next to source as `*.test.ts`. Run `vitest run` in CI and before every commit touching business logic.
- `tsc --noEmit` must pass on every PR.
- Success criterion to verify before launch: New support lead reaches the default queue view in under 2 minutes.
- Success criterion to verify before launch: Role-gated routes deny access with a clear recovery path.
- Success criterion to verify before launch: Queue table handles 10,000 rows through server-side pagination.
- Every data surface has loading, empty, error, and partial states covered.
- Role-gated routes denied with a clear affordance, never a silent 404.
- No PII in client-side logs or analytics payloads.
- Session timeout and re-auth flow tested end-to-end.

## What we are building (from brief)

- Ship a role-aware operations dashboard for support leads within 8 weeks.
- Reduce manual queue triage by surfacing priority accounts and stale cases.
- Give managers exportable weekly metrics without ad-hoc SQL requests.

## Constraints

- Stack is Next.js app router with server actions for mutations.
- Auth comes from the existing SSO provider; no new identity system in v1.
- Tables may include customer names and emails, so analytics and logs must not contain PII.

## Known risks

- Large exports could block the UI unless moved to a background job.
- Permission mistakes are more damaging than missing convenience features.
